speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a psychiatric condition and have developed a new movement disorder; to begin our assessment, have you noticed any specific triggers, such as stress or medication changes, associated with these new movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context; given the schizophrenia diagnosis and recent initiation of risperidone, I want to characterize your movements further. Can you describe the specific type of movement you are experiencing and whether it is involuntary or something you can control? Also, have you noticed any stiffness or tremors in your hands or jaw?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—persistent inner restlessness, fidgeting, and an inability to remain still—are classic signs of akathisia. Given your recent start on risperidone, this is a likely side effect. I need to rule out other causes; have you noticed any muscle stiffness, tremors, or changes in your speech or swallowing recently? Also, have you experienced any fever or confusion?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is very reassuring; the absence of rigidity, tremors, fever, or confusion makes neuroleptic malignant syndrome and other organic causes unlikely. To confirm the diagnosis of risperidone-induced akathisia and assess its severity, how much is this restlessness affecting your daily activities, such as attending classes or sleeping, and would a change in your medication be helpful?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Risperidone-induced Akathisia
